## What the engine does (C1)
- Conditions: the 20 keys of the note (period, hour, weather, place, met, tierMin/tierMax, mood, story, storyDone, gig, gigClient, hired, rankMin, cafe, beat, notBeat, seen, daysSince, recent). An unknown key or a wrongly shaped value never matches (the variant is skipped, the validator reports it).
- Selection per turn: keep matching variants, drop the ones in the person's `last` memory plus this talk's lines, keep the highest score (`w` if given, else number of `if` keys = specificity), pick by `hash(seed, who, node, day, visits, turn)`. If everything was said recently the least recent one returns. Exactly ONE variant (1-3 bubbles) is said per turn, so fragments can never be glued.
- Time: the caller passes the CURRENT (day, minute) in `ctx` on every turn (`chooseReply` builds nothing from a stored time). A talk that crosses 12:00 speaks afternoon lines on the next turn (test pins it).
- Effects are returned as data (`{kind:'meet'|'standing'|'mood'|'beat'|'topic'|'act', amount|id, at:nodeId}`); the engine never touches state. Beats set earlier in a talk are visible to later conditions in the same talk.
- Determinism: only an integer hash; no Math.random, no Date.now, no globals (a test scans the source). Inputs are never mutated (tests pass deep-frozen cast, ctx, mem and session). Garbage never throws in default mode; `{strict:true}` is the test mode that throws on authoring errors (unknown `go`, no entry, nothing to say).

## API for stage C3 (memory) and C6 (wiring)
| Function | Signature | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `talkContext` | `(progress, who, env)`, env = `{day, minute, weather?, place?, seed, recent?:[strings], mem?}` | flat `ctx`: tier (from `progress.standing` via npc-life `tierFor`), mood band (from `progress.npcs[who].mood`), met, story step/done (`progress.starter`), gig type and client (`progress.gigs.active.type/.client`), hired ranks (`progress.careers[id]`), cafe `none/employed/onShift` (`progress.cafe`), beats, seen, daysSince, `mem`. Memory is read from `env.mem`, else `progress.npcs[who].mem`, else `progress.talk.people[who]` (`{metDay,lastDay,last,seen,beats}`). Call it on EVERY turn with the current time. Never throws. |
| `baseContext` | `(patch)` | same ctx from a plain patch (tests, sweeps, talk-check) |
| `openConversation` | `(cast, who, ctx, mem?, {strict}?)` | `{session, lines:[{who,text}], replies:[{id,label,asked}], effects, ended, echo:null, problems:[string]}`. `mem` defaults to `ctx.mem`. |
| `chooseReply` | `(session, cast, replyId, ctx, mem?, {strict}?)` | same shape plus `echo:{who:'you',text:label}` for the transcript. `replyId` from the last `replies`; `BYE_ID` ('bye', label "See you") is always offered and ends the talk (plays `cast.bye` if present). An unknown id returns the same replies and `problems`, no state change. |
| `remember` | `(mem, session)` | NEW mem `{last (6), seen (32 keys), beats (16), lastMin}`. Call ONCE when the talk ends, including when the player walks away. It is not idempotent (visit counts add up), so do not call it every turn. |
| `cleanMem`, `freshMem` | `(raw)`, `()` | normaliser and empty memory; C3's `normalizeTalkMem` can wrap `cleanMem` (same caps and shape as note 2f). |
| `lineKey` | `(text)` | short base-36 hash; the memory stores one key per VARIANT (hash of its joined bubbles), not per bubble. |
| `matches`, `specificity`, `effectsOf`, `bubblesOf`, `expand`, `indexNodes`, `entryNodes`, `periodOf`, `hourOf` | helpers (also used by the validator) | exported constants: `CONDITION_KEYS, EFFECT_KEYS, PERIODS, TIERS, MOOD_BANDS, PLACES, WEATHERS, CAFE_STATES, MAX_REPLIES (6), MAX_BUBBLES (3), MAX_BUBBLE_CHARS (160), BYE_ID, BYE_LABEL` |

What C6 must do with it, in order, each reply or time step:
1. `ctx = talkContext(progress, who, {day:hudDay(), minute:hudMinutes(), seed:MAP.seed, place, recent:recentEvents()})`, then `openConversation(castOf(who), who, ctx)`.
2. On each reply click: rebuild `ctx` with the CURRENT time, `chooseReply(session, cast, id, ctx)`. Show `echo`, `lines`, `replies` (dim `asked`). Keep `session` (plain JSON).
3. Apply each `effects[i]` in order: `meet` sets npc.metDay (and `progress.talk.people` entry for non-roster people), `standing` goes through `gainStanding` (+3/day cap), `mood` and `topic` through npc-life `talk`/mood rules, `beat` is already tracked in the session and stored by `remember`, `act` goes through the ACTS map to the existing game functions. An `act` reply with no `go` ends the talk (`ended:true`).
4. When `ended` is true or the player walks more than 3 m away: `mem = remember(mem, session)` and write it to `progress.npcs[who].mem` or `progress.talk.people[who]` (C3 owns the save format and caps; note `normalizeNpcs` currently drops unknown fields, so `mem` is lost on reload until C3 teaches it).

## What the validator does (C2)
`validateCast(cast, {acts, others, ids, places, sweepLimit})` returns `[{rule, code, level, who, node, where, text, message, fix}]`; `validateCasts(casts, opts)` checks every cast against the rest (cross-cast repeated lines). `message` is `"<Person> / node <id> / <where>: <what is wrong>. Fix: <how>."`, written so a model can correct its own content from the text alone. Codes by rule:
1 `unknown-condition`, `bad-condition-value`, `unknown-effect`, `unknown-act` | 2 `unreachable-node` | 3 `dead-end` | 4 `missing-go` | 5 `too-many-replies` | 6 `duplicate-label` | 7 `repeated-text` (normalised, this cast and other casts) | 8 `wrong-time-word` (variant's period set from `if` AND node `when`, including `hour` ranges; "tomorrow morning", "last night", "mornings" ignored) | 9 `glue-suspect` (two greeting openers in a variant; a bubble starting lower-case or not ending in . ! ? or an ellipsis) | 10 `line-too-long` (bubble over 160, label over 60), `placeholder-text` (undefined/null/NaN/braces/TODO, unknown `{slot}`, raw ids from `opts.ids` or the cast's own ids, `word.word` leaks) | 11 `uncovered-node` (sweep: a reachable node, or the entry set, with no variant for some hour x tier x mood x story x place x gig x rank x cafe x beat x recent combination it can be reached in).
Extras (rule 0): `bad-shape`, `duplicate-node-id`, `no-entry`, `crowd-facts` (cast `kind:'crowd'` needs facts job, home, hint), `missing-voice`, and the cheap per-person voice checks `voice-avoid` (optional `cast.avoid:[words]`) and `voice-sentence-long` (optional `cast.maxSentenceWords`), both warnings.

`scripts/talk-check.mjs <module> [personId] [--period --tier --place --mood --story --story-done --day --seed --met --walk --acts --places --problems-only]` prints the problem list and one transcript block per period x tier (with `--walk`, every reply 3 levels deep, with effects). Exit code 1 on errors, 2 on load errors. Usage is in its header comment. It accepts any module whose exports contain a cast, an array of casts or an object of casts, and a bare person id once `dist/cast.js` exists (needs `castOf(id)`), which does not exist yet.

## Deviations from the design note (all small)
1. **`entry:true` flag.** The note's example node (`noah.open`) has no marker for "can start a talk". I added `entry:true` (entry nodes are filtered by `when`, most specific `when` first, then hash). Validator rule `no-entry` enforces at least one.
2. **`openConversation` also returns `effects`, `problems`, `echo`; `chooseReply` returns `echo`.** Needed so the first node's `meet`/`beat` effects are applied and the player's choice can be shown. `remember` also writes `<who>.first` when a `meet` effect fired (so `met` is true next time).
3. **Memory is one key per VARIANT**, not per bubble (a 3-bubble variant would otherwise use half of the 6 slots).
4. **`{name}` fact slots** in text are expanded from `cast.facts` (crowd templates in C9 need them); the validator flags unknown slots.
5. **`reply.act` without `go` ends the talk** (the act opens its own menu); a `go` to a missing node at runtime hides that reply instead of dead-ending, and reports it in `problems`.
6. **Rule 8 does not check the word "late"** (too ambiguous: "too late", "running late"); words checked are in `TIME_WORDS`. Time words in reply labels are not checked.
7. Rule 11's sweep uses the places named in the cast's conditions plus `opts.places`; it cannot know where the game lets you talk to a person, so a counter-only person passes unless the caller lists other places.
8. `mood` condition is a band name (miserable/low/okay/good/delighted), taken from npc-life `moodWord`; `talkContext` imports `tierFor` and `moodWord` from `dist/npc-life.js` (pure, existing).

## What I could NOT verify
- Nothing here runs in the game: no cast files exist, game.js is untouched, so the whole API is verified only against inline test casts and the real `npc-life.js` tier/mood functions.
- The `progress` field names read by `talkContext` (`starter.step/done/skipped`, `gigs.active.type/client`, `careers[id].hired/rank`, `cafe.employed/stage`, `standing.people`, `npcs[id].mood/metDay/mem`, `talk.people[id]`) come from reading `starter.js`, `gigs.js`, `careers.js`, `cafe-job.js`, `npc-life.js`; I did not run them against a real saved profile.
- `talk-check.mjs` module loading by bare person id (via `dist/cast.js`) is untested because that file does not exist yet.
- Performance of the sweep on a large real cast (30+ nodes with many condition keys); it is capped at 4000 contexts per node (`SWEEP_LIMIT`) and the three small casts in the tests run in well under a second.
- The validator's time-word, glue and id heuristics are cheap regexes; they will have some false positives on real prose (for example a capitalised proper noun at the start of a lower-case continuation, or "night" used metaphorically). Treat the first Gemini runs as tuning.

## Confidence
- Engine selection, determinism, memory, effects, garbage safety: high (every behaviour pinned by a test, including 8 variants x 25 talks with no repeat inside the last 6).
- Validator rules 1-10 and message quality: high for the rule semantics, medium for how well the regexes behave on real content.
- Rule 11 sweep: medium-high; exhaustive within its listed domains but the domains are inferred from the cast's own conditions.
- talk-check script: medium-high (programmatic and process-style runs tested through `main`, not through a shell exit code in CI).
- `talkContext` against real progress shapes: medium (see above).
